name: Pete Hegseth
role: US Secretary of Defense / War (2025-), former Fox News host and Army National Guard officer
summary: Hegseth is a strongly conservative, Christian-identified Trump ally who opposes globalism, DEI and what he calls woke politics. He favors a more lethal military with fewer legal constraints, tariffs, a border wall, strong support for Israel and a restructured NATO. Several of his positions are drawn from secondary summaries of his books and speeches.

notes:
Women in combat: said in 2024 they should not serve, then at his 2025 hearing said standards matter more (s5); answered under distinct-gender-roles using the later hearing and Secretary-era position (recency rule). Marriage and abortion positions date from 2012 and 2002. Much of the book content comes via Wikipedia summaries, not the book itself. war.gov transcripts returned HTTP 403, so no official primary page could be opened; s4 (CNN transcript of his speech) remains the only primary source.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 32 answers taken from it, 31 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: The 2024 book predates his 2025 appointment; later statements and actions were checked and the most recent clear position used (for example, women in combat: 'straight up no' in November 2024, but standards-based at the January 2025 hearing and in Secretary policy). Several positions on American Crusade (2020) rest on Wikipedia's quotation of that book rather than the text itself, so they are capped at medium. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind; his book The War on Warriors (local library copy) is read by theme and cited; eleven answers that rested only on Wikipedia pages are nulled where the book and speeches hold no statement, with review history. MediaSum holds 35 of his television and radio appearances (2007-2020: Iraq and Afghanistan surges, sequestration, veterans); read for guns, entitlements, trade and immigration. The 2025 House Armed Services and Appropriations hearings (his turns as Secretary) and the full text of American Crusade (2020, archive.org) were read by theme; the nulled statements are those on which neither those, the 2024 book nor MediaSum hold a position (same-sex marriage, reduce-immigration as a whole, land-for-peace). Searched in the 2024 book without a settled answer: guns, same-sex marriage, trade, tariffs, Israel, religion in schools, capital punishment, democracy, nuclear weapons, NATO.
